rows.name: Nonlinear bulk streaming in sub-millimeter dielectric channels
rows.required_subsystems: MHz-class phased-array driving electronics; sub-millimeter (0.3–0.8 mm hydraulic diameter) chemically inert channel manifolds; fluorinated-ketone dielectric coolant handling
rows.physical_effects: Acoustic-radiation-pressure-driven steady streaming; nonlinear harmonic momentum deposition; cavitation-microjet ejection suppressed (saturation-limited regime); bulk recirculation at acoustic Mach number ≥ 0.05
rows.enabling_technologies: Lab-scale MHz focused ultrasound bulk-streaming rigs (e.g., NIH/Utah focused-ultrasound drug-delivery platforms operating 1–5 MHz in aqueous media ≥1 mm channels); fluorinated-ketone dielectric coolants 3M Novec 7000/7100/7200 series with measured η ≈ 0.7–1.2 mPa·s and saturation pressure ≈ 1 atm at 25 °C; no published demonstration of streaming in sub-mm hydraulic-diameter channels with fluorinated ketone at Ma ≥ 0.05
rows.exists_today_basis: Today: bulk acoustic streaming demonstrated in water/tissue at 1–5 MHz in channels ≥1–2 mm (Rumpler, Pennathur lab; Wiklund; Dual-layer ultrasound pumping); fluorinated ketones (Novec 7000/7100/7200) confirmed η ≈ 0.7–1.2 mPa·s at 25 °C but saturation pressure ≈ 1 atm at 25 °C falls below the ≥1 atm at 60 °C required by the 2055 spec; sub-mm (0.3–0.8 mm) channel streaming with dielectric coolant at Ma ≥ 0.05 is unreported

rows.name: MHz-class high-power-density GaN-on-diamond phased-array transducers
rows.required_subsystems: 1–5 MHz GaN-on-diamond RF power die; diamond heat-spreader bonded with ≤5 K·W⁻¹ junction-to-channel thermal resistance; ≤3 mm × 3 mm array elements with phased-array beamforming ASICs; impedance-matched fluorinated-ketone acoustic load
rows.physical_effects: Piezoelectric transduction at 1–5 MHz continuous wave; phased electronic beam steering/focusing; thermal extraction through polycrystalline or single-crystal diamond into dielectric coolant
rows.enabling_technologies: Akhan Semiconductor/Stanford/MIT Lincoln Lab GaN-on-diamond HEMT wafers (pulsed 0.6 W·mm⁻² at 2–3 GHz RF, not 1–5 MHz acoustic); Blatek/Onda piezoelectric PZT phased-array therapy heads (1–3 MHz, ≈0.05–0.1 W·mm⁻² continuous into tissue); Element Six/Raytech CVD diamond bonding with measured thermal resistance 5–10 K·W⁻¹; Acoustic Wave Therapy/Verasonics research phased arrays at 1–5 MHz with element pitch ≥5 mm
rows.exists_today_basis: Today: highest demonstrated continuous acoustic surface power density at 1–5 MHz is ~0.05–0.1 W·mm⁻² (therapy HIFU / Verasonics research arrays); GaN-on-diamond is qualified only at RF (GHz) and only pulsed, never at 1–5 MHz continuous acoustic output; junction-to-channel thermal resistance ≤5 K·W⁻¹ into a fluorinated-ketone dielectric coolant has not been published; required ≥1.0 W·mm⁻² continuous at 1–5 MHz into a sub-mm channel is roughly 10–20× beyond any reported MHz-class acoustic phased array

rows.name: Dimensionally consistent Nusselt correlation for bulk-streaming-dominated convection in sub-mm channels
rows.required_subsystems: Calibrated MHz phased-array rigs with 0.3–0.8 mm hydraulic-diameter channels; dielectric-coolant thermophysical property database; spatially-resolved temperature/holographic PIV across the bulk (not boundary-layer); Re, Re_ac,bulk, Pr dimensionless framework with Re_ac,bulk defined on D_h
rows.physical_effects: Reynolds-number scaling of bulk-streaming convective transport; Re_ac,bulk definition on hydraulic diameter; saturation-limited (δ_ac > δ_BL) transition criterion; spatially-averaged h_eff closure valid at Ma ≥ 0.05
rows.enabling_technologies: Classical Sieder-Tate, Gnielinski, and Shah-London correlations for forced convection in mm-to-cm tubes (no acoustic term); acoustic-streaming Nusselt literature limited to δ_ac-based or boundary-layer-local formulations (Vainshtein, Moshkin, Wiklund) with no D_h-based Re_ac,bulk closure; no published correlation spanning Ma ≥ 0.05, D_h = 0.3–0.8 mm, Pr ≈ 10–20 fluorinated-ketone range
rows.exists_today_basis: Today: no validated Nusselt correlation of the form Nu = f(Re, Re_ac,bulk, Pr) with Re_ac,bulk built on hydraulic diameter exists; existing acoustic-convection literature uses viscous boundary-layer (δ_ac) length scales and is dimensionally inconsistent when applied to 0.3–0.8 mm channels; the required closure has not been published in peer-reviewed heat-transfer, microfluidics, or acoustic-streaming journals as of 2026

rows.name: Sub-cm/sub-s heat-flux tomography at ≥10⁴ voxels/m³ and ≤0.1 s temporal resolution
rows.required_subsystems: Cryogenic bolometer arrays, phosphor-thermometric meshes, MHz-rate tomographic inversion ASICs, cell-pouch-embedded routing
rows.physical_effects: Cryogenic bolometric resistance change vs. incident radiative/acoustic power; phosphor thermometry via temperature-dependent luminescence decay; inverse heat-conduction/streaming reconstruction
rows.enabling_technologies: Cryo-CMOS bolometer ROICs (e.g., NIST/IRAM 2024 sub-K TES arrays at 10³–10⁴ pixels per focal plane); phosphor thermometry demonstrated on turbine blades (Liu et al., 2023, ~10² points, ~0.1 s); real-time algebraic reconstruction at MHz is only in medical CT (Siemens Force, ~5×10³ projections/s, macroscopic scale)
rows.exists_today_basis: Existing cryogenic bolometer focal planes reach ~10⁴ pixels per plane but are not reconstructed as 3-D volumetric heat-flux tomograms at 0.1 s; phosphor thermography yields ~10²–10³ surface points at ~10 Hz; no volumetric 10⁴ voxels/m³ at 0.1 s has been demonstrated — required voxel density exceeds today's surface-mapped thermography by ~2 orders of magnitude and required temporal resolution exceeds phosphor decay-limited schemes by ~10×

rows.name: GaN-on-diamond phased LRAD at ≥2.5 W/cm² continuous acoustic intensity at 500 Hz from a <3 mm thick element
rows.required_subsystems: GaN-on-diamond RF MEMS transducer array, sub-3 mm diaphragm/spacer stack, phase-locked drive electronics, HIC enclosure
rows.physical_effects: Wide-bandwidth GaN piezoelectric actuation; diamond as high-thermal-conductivity heat spreader for continuous-wave operation; phased-array beamforming at 100–1000 Hz
rows.enabling_technologies: Bulk PZT tonpilz projectors (e.g., Neptune Sonar DUK-EN) achieve ~0.3–0.8 W/cm² at 300–1000 Hz from 20–40 mm stacks; cMUT/PMUT arrays deliver <0.1 W/cm²; AlN-on-Si phased panels (USSI, 2022) ~0.05 W/cm² at 1 kHz from ~1.5 mm stacks; GaN-on-diamond continuous acoustic output has been characterized for heat-spreading (DARPA ICECool, 2023) but not phased acoustic transduction in this geometry
rows.exists_today_basis: No published GaN-on-diamond phased array has demonstrated ≥2.5 W/cm² continuous acoustic intensity at 500 Hz from <3 mm thickness; best bulk piezo devices reach ~0.8 W/cm² but from 20–40 mm stacks, and AlN/PMUT thin-film arrays are ~30× below the required continuous intensity

rows.name: On-pouch cryogenic bolometer/phosphor mesh with areal density ≤5×10⁻⁴ g/cm² and acoustic impedance mismatch ΔZ <2%
rows.required_subsystems: Thin-film superconducting bolometer mesh, phosphor thermometric film, acoustically transparent interconnects, roll-to-roll 2D-material lamination onto pouch laminate
rows.physical_effects: Superconducting transition thermometry at cryogenic cell temperature; phosphor luminescence decay thermometry; acoustic impedance matching via sub-wavelength porous/2D-mesh membranes
rows.enabling_technologies: Graphene/2D-material aerogel meshes (MIT/HZG, 2023) at ~10⁻³ g/cm² but with ΔZ >20% to air; ultrathin SiNx bolometer membranes (NASA/GSFC, 2022) ~5×10⁻⁴ g/cm² but fabricated as discrete 100–500 µm pixels, not continuous meshes; phosphor-thermometric paints (Kitagawa et al., 2024) require ~0.02 g/cm² binder layers and are acoustically opaque
rows.exists_today_basis: No demonstrated mesh simultaneously meets ≤5×10⁻⁴ g/cm² areal density and ΔZ <2% to the cell-pouch acoustic medium; existing 2D-material membranes are acoustically transparent (ΔZ <5%) but are 2–5× too massive per area, and existing cryogenic bolometer pixels are discrete with acoustic-impedance discontinuities >10%

Lyapunov-stable higher-order sliding-mode controller execution on edge AI with <50 ms deterministic loop latency | Industrial-temperature-grade embedded processor (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson Orin, Intel Xeon D-1500, or ARM Cortex-A78 cluster), deterministic real-time OS (VxWorks, QNX, or PREEMPT_RT Linux),

rows.name: Online extended Kalman filter for stiff exothermic kinetics with κ(J) < 10⁴ at operating point
rows.required_subsystems: Multi-variate spectroscopic state observer (Raman + NIR + possibly FTIR), covariance matrix propagation (P_k) with Joseph stabilized update, automatic differentiation or analytic Jacobian of 4-6 state ODEs (T, C_A, C_B, possibly C_catalyst, wall-T), square-root or UD-factorized EKF to preserve numerical conditioning, dual estimation or joint EKF-MHE scheme for joint state-parameter identification
rows.physical_effects: Jacobian condition number κ(J) = σ_max(J)/σ_min(J) governed by observability Gramian; stiff exothermic CSTR Jacobian entries ∂r_i/∂T ~ E_a/RT² · k₀·exp(-E_a/RT)·C_A^n, which for E_a = 100 kJ/mol at T = 350 K gives ∂r/∂T ~ 10³-10⁴, and combined with multi-species coupling yields κ(J) ~ 10⁵-10⁷; EKF covariance update requires κ(P) to remain < 10⁸ to avoid filter divergence; reducing κ(J) to <10⁴ requires either (a) multi-variate spectroscopy adding 3-6 independent concentration measurements instead of single T, or (b) explicit model reduction via singular perturbation / quasi-steady-state assumption (QSSA); today's industrial reactor state estimation uses extended Kalman filters, moving-horizon estimators (MHE), and unscented Kalman filters on AspenTech DMCplus or Honeywell Unisim with state vectors typically 3-6 and κ(J) accepted at 10⁵-10⁶ via regularization, but multi-variate spectroscopic EKF on industrial CSTRs at 10 Hz is demonstrated only in research papers (e.g., Rodrigues et al. 2015, São João et al. 2017 for spectroscopic EKF on mini-plant reactors), not as commercial product
rows.enabling_technologies: exists today: partial
rows.exists_today: today's demonstrated ekf/mhe state estimation on industrial cstrs achieves 1-10 hz update on 4-6 state models with κ(j) typically 10⁵-10⁷ tolerated via tikhonov regularization (e.g., dow chemical polymerization reactor observers in academic collaborations, perrier & de assis brazil miniplant papers on spectroscopic ekf for ethanol reactor); κ(j) < 10⁴ with single-temperature observability is not achievable for stiff autocatalytic/polymerization systems because the fisher information matrix rank-deficient, and multi-variate spectroscopic ekf achieving κ(j) < 10⁴ has been demonstrated only on laboratory microreactors and pilot plants, not on industrial-scale cstrs with optical-access constraints
rows.exists_today_basis: operating regime match: no
rows.operating_regime_match: the required κ(j) < 10⁴ on a 4-6 state stiff exothermic cstr jacobian at industrial operating point is not demonstrated today with single-temperature measurement (demonstrated κ(j) is 10⁵-10⁷), and the alternative of multi-variate spectroscopic ekf achieving κ(j) < 10⁴ has been demonstrated only on laboratory microreactors, not on industrial cstrs meeting the boundary conditions (slurry, optical access, exothermic 50-150 kj/mol)

Wireless passive MEMS pressure sensor array embeddable inside a fluid-filled shell-side lattice, ±5 Pa accuracy over 0-50 kPa, ≤5 mm³ package, 220 °C continuous operation, ≥10-year survivability in hot water/dielectric oil | Capacitive or piezoresistive MEMS pressure sensing with wireless (inductive

Topology-optimization solver coupling Navier-Stokes, conjugate heat transfer, Darcy–Forchheimer, and additive-manufacturability constraints over ~10⁶ design variables with <5% residual convergence in ≤8 h on commodity HPC | High-throughput CFD topology optimization using adjoint methods, lattice-Bol

rows.name: Coaxial cryogenic tool-holder flow integrity
rows.required_subsystems: Vacuum-insulated tool shank, coaxial LN2 inlet through spindle/tool interface, two-phase flow management at rake face, mass-flow controller with proportional valve
rows.physical_effects: LN2 film-boiling heat transfer above Leidenfrost flux, two-phase flow metering, vapor-quality preservation through insulated delivery, phase-change heat extraction at tool-chip interface
rows.enabling_technologies: Additive-manufactured vacuum-insulated cryogenic transfer lines (e.g., NASA/Blue Origin cryogenic feedlines, KAWAHARA Vacuum-Jacketed Tooling research), proportional mass-flow controllers for LN2 (Bronkhorst EL-FLOW, M+W Instruments), external cryogenic nozzle assemblies on CNC lathes (5-axis MagForge LN2 retrofit, CryoCrest systems); demonstrated LN2 flow rates through tool shanks remain in the 0.2–0.4 L/min range with external nozzle injection (e.g., literature on cryogenic machining of Ti-6Al-4V by Dhar & Kamruzzaman, UMIST cold-spray experiments)
rows.exists_today_basis: Today's external-nozzle LN2 delivery achieves ~0.3 L/min with 20–35% vapor fraction at the rake face; AM vacuum-jacketed shanks have been demonstrated at TRL 4 for static cryogenic delivery (no rotating spindle integration with 1.5+ L/min and <5% vapor quality); no published demonstration of >1.0 L/min single-phase LN2 through a rotating CNC tool-holder spindle seal

rows.name: Embedded thin-film cryogenic temperature sensing in cutting tools
rows.required_subsystems: Thin-film Pt/Au deposition on WC/PCD tool substrate, lead routing through tool body, 10 kHz data acquisition with cold-junction compensation, high-cycle thermomechanical fatigue resistance at rake face
rows.physical_effects: Thermoelectric Seebeck effect at thin-film junction, thin-film adhesion under cyclic thermal shock (70–1000 K), low-thermal-mass heat-sinking, electromagnetic-noise-immune signal conditioning
rows.enabling_technologies: Sputter-deposited Pt-RTD thin-film sensors on metal substrates (Heraeus Pt1000 chip elements, IST AG thin-film Pt sensors rated to 600 °C with ~10⁵ cycle thermal-shock data); embedded thermocouples in cutting tools demonstrated in turning inserts (SANDVIK CoroCut, research by Klocke/MPIP at RWTH Aachen) but using embedded K-type wires at 1 kHz; no published 10 kHz thin-film Pt/Au thermocouple operating continuously at 70 K rake-face temperature with 10⁶-cycle validated life
rows.exists_today_basis: Thin-film Pt RTDs (Heraeus, IST) operate to 600 °C with ±0.3 K accuracy at low sample rates and ~10⁵ thermal cycles; no demonstrated operation at 70 K on a rotating WC tool with 10⁶-cycle fatigue and 10 kHz acquisition free of calibration drift; cryogenic thin-film Cernox sensors (Lakeshore) reach 0.1 K accuracy at 70 K but are not rake-face-embedded in WC tools

rows.name: Adaptive CNC controller with real-time cryogenic loop closure
rows.required_subsystems: CNC with high-speed PLC/Motion-Control fieldbus (EtherCAT/SERCOS), cryogenic-specific PID loop on tool-tip temperature, mass-flow proportional valve actuation, sub-50 ms thermal feedback loop, integration with spindle load/cutting-force sensors
rows.physical_effects: PID feedback control on tool-tip temperature, feedforward from spindle current/feed-force, real-time thermal model of tool-chip interface, valve hysteresis compensation
rows.enabling_technologies: Industrial CNC controllers (FANUC Series 30i/31i, Siemens SINUMERIK ONE, Heidenhain TNC 640) provide 1–4 ms servo loop time but thermal-control loops remain slow; cryogenic-MFC add-on systems (Cryojet proportional-valve retrofits, Praxair/LINDE cryogenic machining controllers) operate at 100–250 ms with ~0.2 L/min MFC resolution (Bronkhorst EL-FLOW Prestige at 1:2000 turndown gives ±0.005 L/min, but only when not thermally disturbed); no published CNC with sub-50 ms closed-loop cryogenic flux control tied directly to an in-tool thermocouple during turning
rows.exists_today_basis: Modern CNC motion controllers achieve sub-4 ms servo latency (FANUC 30i, Siemens ONE) and Bronkhorst EL-FLOW mass-flow controllers achieve 0.05 L/min resolution with ~50 ms valve response, but no integrated system closes a tool-tip-temperature feedback loop within 50 ms during a live turning cut at 60–180 m/min; current cryogenic machining retrofits are open-loop or slow-feedback (250+ ms)

rows.name: On-die junction temperature sensing (TSEP) at 1 kHz per-leg with ±2 °C accuracy
rows.required_subsystems: Per-leg TSEP structure (on-state VCE/VDS or gate-threshold TSEP), gate-driver-embedded ADC sampling channel per switch position, calibration against self-heating transients
rows.physical_effects: Thermo-sensitive electrical parameter (TSEP) shifting with junction temperature; thermal time constant of GaN/SiC die allowing kHz-band estimation; per-leg synchronization via shared timebase
rows.enabling_technologies: Infineon EiceDRIVER 1ED34xx family with integrated DESAT/AIN for Tj estimation on SiC modules; Analog Devices ADuM4146 gate driver with on-board temperature channel; Wolfspeed WolfPACK modules using NTC + thermal-model Tj estimators operating at hundreds of Hz, not kHz; published University of Nottingham/EPFL TSEP demos on GaN HEMTs at MHz sampling but only single-pulse validation, not continuous per-leg at drive ratings
rows.exists_today_basis: Today: TSEP demonstrated on discrete GaN/SiC devices in laboratory fixtures (e.g., 1 MHz VDS(on) sampling on 650 V GaN HEMTs by Chen et al., IEEE TPEL 2023) at ±3–5 °C accuracy; commercial SiC modules ship with NTC thermistor plus behavioral thermal model (Infineon, Wolfspeed, ON Semi) producing ~100 Hz Tj estimate at ±5 °C; no commercial or published per-leg 1 kHz synchronous Tj stream at ±2 °C on a drive-rated 50–100 kVA module

rows.name: Model-predictive control solved in <25 µs on inverter MCU/DSP
rows.required_subsystems: Floating-point MPC solver with horizon ≥ N switching events, explicit horizon cost function on E_sw·exp(α·Tj), sub-period scheduling output
rows.physical_effects: Finite-control-set MPC discrete enumeration of switching states; cost-function evaluation on FPGA/DSP with parallel MAC; floating-point arithmetic at MHz core clocks
rows.enabling_technologies: Texas Instruments C2000 F28P65x and TMS320F2838x running finite-set MPC at 50–100 µs solve latency on 2-level 3-phase inverters (TI app note SPRABK5, 2018); Microchip dsPIC33CH dual-core with 25–40 µs MPC reported in 2022 PE demos; FPGA-implemented MPC (Xilinx Zynq, Altera Cyclone) reaching 1–5 µs horizon solve but at small horizon length and without per-leg Tj cost term; published IEEE TPEL 2024 demonstrations of horizon-1 FCS-MPC at switching frequency up to 100 kHz on GaN converters
rows.exists_today_basis: Today: 50–100 µs MPC solve on C2000/Microchip DSPs (documented for 2-level 3-phase drives, fixed cost terms); 1–5 µs horizon solve on FPGA but horizon limited to 1–2 steps and cost function lacks the ΔTj-weighted E_sw·exp(α·Tj) term; the combined requirement of sub-25 µs solve WITH per-leg Tj-horizon cost on a drive-rated DSP/MCU is not commercially shipped or peer-reviewed demonstrated

rows.name: SiC/GaN inverter module cost <0.05 $/VA at 50–100 kVA rating
rows.required_subsystems: Wafer-level SiC MOSFET or GaN HEMT die at <0.02 $/VA; low-inductance module packaging (Kelvin source, silver-sinter die attach); integrated gate-driver co-pack
rows.physical_effects: Wide-bandgap semiconductor with high breakdown field (SiC 3 MV/cm, GaN 3.3 MV/cm); low on-resistance per unit area (Rds(on)·A figures of merit); silver-sinter bonding for thermomechanical reliability
rows.enabling_technologies: Wolfspeed XM3/E3 SiC MOSFET modules at 0.10–0.15 $/VA in 2024 (Wolfspeed product datasheets, 1200 V/300–600 A); Infineon CoolSiC EasyPACK and EasyDUAL at similar ASP for 50–100 kVA traction/inverter ratings; GaN Systems GS-065 series at 650 V/60 A priced around 0.20 $/VA at module level; OEM traction inverter pricing (Tesla, Lucid, BYD) reported at 0.08–0.12 $/VA for SiC at 100–200 kVA
rows.exists_today_basis: Today: SiC modules at 0.10–0.15 $/VA for 50–100 kVA ratings (Wolfspeed, Infineon, onsemi published 2024 distributor pricing); GaN at 0.18–0.25 $/VA at 650 V/≤60 A; no commercial or foundry-priced SiC/GaN product at <0.05 $/VA in this rating class, and Yole Group 2023 power SiC market report projects 0.04–0.06 $/VA only by ~2032 under aggressive learning-curve assumptions

rows.name: MR-fluid bearing yield stress in field-operable envelope
rows.required_subsystems: Magnetorheological fluid chamber integrated into spherical-roller bearing raceway lubrication gap; electromagnet coils or permanent-magnet rotor providing H-field across shear zone; temperature-stable MR fluid chemistry
rows.physical_effects: Magnetic polarization of ferromagnetic particles forming chain-like structures that increase yield stress under field (Bingham plastic behavior); shear yield stress scales with H^1.5 in magnetorheological fluids; stable viscosity across -20 to +45 C
rows.enabling_technologies: LORD MRF-2 fluid (yield ~30-50 kPa, but degrades sharply below 0 C), MR grease formulations by QinetiQ/Schaeffler for wind turbine pitch bearings (~10-20 kPa below freezing), experimental carbonyl-iron MR fluids at lab scale
rows.exists_today_basis: QinetiQ/Schaeffler MR-grease pitch-bearing demos on multi-MW turbines operate continuously at -10 to +40 C with ~15-25 kPa yield stress; LORD MRF-132DG reaches ~60 kPa only at +40 to +80 C with viscosity >0.5 Pa.s; no public demonstration of >=50 kPa yield stress sustained at -20 C and <=0.3 Pa.s simultaneously in a rolling-element bearing
rows.operating_regime_match: no (operating regime mismatch: required >=50 kpa at -20 c with low viscosity, demonstrated ~15-25 kpa at -20 c and ~60 kpa only at high temperature with high viscosity — neither regime is jointly satisfied today)

rows.name: Embedded FBG strain sensing with model-predictive control at required bandwidth
rows.required_subsystems: Fiber-Bragg grating arrays bonded or embedded in bearing race/inner ring; interrogator with high-speed swept-laser or swept-wavelength source; wireless or non-contact (inductive/RF) telemetry across rotor-stator gap; edge processor running MPC at kHz rate; piezo-hydraulic actuator driver receiving control setpoints
rows.physical_effects: Bragg wavelength shift with strain (dlambda/lambda ~ 0.78 x epsilon); high-speed spectral demodulation; real-time optimization via receding-horizon model-predictive control
rows.enabling_technologies: Micron Optics sm130/sm900 interrogators (1-10 kHz sampling, 1-5 microstrain resolution), Luna Innovations ODiSI (100 Hz-1 kHz), FBGS Technologies Draw Tower Grating arrays for wind blade sensing (10-100 Hz, ~50 microstrain), Siemens/Kistler telemetry in rotating machinery via slip rings, Acuity AR2000 distance lasers for rotor position; MPC libraries (MATLAB/MOSEK) at kHz on industrial PLCs
rows.exists_today_basis: Micron Optics sm130 achieves 1 kHz at ~5 microstrain in benchtop and wind-blade FBG demos (FBGS/FIBERSENSING), and industrial MPC loops run at 1-5 kHz on Beckhoff CX-series PLCs; however, demonstrated end-to-end latency including non-contact rotor-to-stator telemetry is 50-200 ms via slip rings (e.g., HBM/SKALA slip-ring telemetry in wind main shafts), and no public demonstration shows <=50 ms end-to-end with >1 kHz sample rate across a rotating main shaft in a multi-MW turbine
rows.operating_regime_match: no (operating regime mismatch: required <=50 ms end-to-end latency with >1 khz fbg sample rate, demonstrated 50-200 ms latency limited by slip-ring telemetry at 10-100 hz effective rate)

rows.name: Shaft-mounted piezo-hydraulic actuation for contact-angle adjustment
rows.required_subsystems: Piezoelectric stack actuator coupled to hydraulic amplification stage (intensifier) mounted in main bearing housing; local hydraulic reservoir and proportional valve; power electronics and wireless power receive coil on rotating shaft; thermal management on rotor
rows.physical_effects: Piezoelectric strain (d33 mode) driving hydraulic piston for force amplification; closed-loop servo control of preload force; contact-angle change via roller-race kinematics
rows.enabling_technologies: Moog/Enidine piezo-hydraulic shutters for aerospace vibration mounts (~5-20 kN dynamic force, 0.5-2 kW), CEDRAT Technologies PPA series piezo actuators with hydraulic amplification (~10-30 kN, benchtop), Bosch Rexroth/HAWE piezo-proportional valves (prototype), Parker LORD fluidlastic mounts with piezo trim
rows.exists_today_basis: CEDRAT PPA80M actuators demonstrate ~20-30 kN dynamic force in benchtop characterization at <1 kW, and Moog flight-qualified piezo-hydraulic mounts operate at ~10-15 kN continuous on helicopter rotor heads (rotor speeds 200-400 rpm, ambient -40 to +85 C); however, no commercial or demonstrated unit achieves >=50 kN dynamic preload authority within a <=0.05 m^3 package qualified for mounting on a multi-MW wind turbine main shaft (shaft speeds 5-18 rpm, ambient -20 to +45 C, radial space constraint from bearing housing)
rows.operating_regime_match: no (operating regime mismatch: required >=50 kn dynamic authority in <=0.05 m^3 on a 5-18 rpm main shaft, demonstrated ~15-30 kn at aerospace vibration-mount packaging with no wind-turbine main-shaft qualification or temperature/space validation)

rows.name: Photochromic-MOF photostability under repeated trans/cis cycling
rows.required_subsystems: Zr-O secondary building units (UiO-66 topology), azobenzene-4,4'-dicarboxylate linkers, defect-engineered node vacancies, hydrophobic pore functionalization
rows.physical_effects: Reversible photoisomerization (trans-to-cis N=N), framework mechanical tolerance to ~3 Å pore-aperture swing, suppressed photobleaching via ligand rigidity
rows.enabling_technologies: Azobenzene-UiO-66 thin films reported with ~200 trans/cis cycles before amorphization (ACS Nano 2024); related azobenzene-functionalized UiO-66 and MIL-53 analogues show similar fatigue limits under 365 nm irradiation
rows.exists_today_basis: Highest reported cycling durability of azobenzene-Zr-MOF composites is ~200 cycles before measurable BET surface area loss, far short of the >1000-cycle requirement

rows.name: Visible-light-driven CO2 photoelectron transfer at framework metal site with sub-10 ns transfer time
rows.required_subsystems: Zr-oxo node chromophore, linker-to-metal charge-transfer excited state, framework-bound CO2•- adduct stabilization, PCET with co-adsorbed H2O
rows.physical_effects: Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT), intervalence electron hopping, surface-bound CO2•- radical intermediate, proton-coupled electron transfer yielding surface formate/oxalate
rows.enabling_technologies: Best reported Zr-MOF chromophore systems (e.g., Zr-MOF-808 with Ru/Re photosensitizer guests) exhibit photoinduced electron transfer to bound substrates at ~10⁷-10⁸ s-¹; direct CO2•- adduct formation on node-confined CO2 has not been spectroscopically confirmed at this rate
rows.exists_today_basis: Electron-transfer rates of 10⁷-10⁸ s-¹ have been measured in Zr-MOF chromophore systems with bound substrates, but specifically CO2 photoelectron transfer at framework metal sites yielding a stabilized CO2•- adduct with subsequent PCET to formate/oxalate has not been demonstrated under flue-gas-relevant conditions

rows.name: Solar concentrator flux at 400 nm deployable on flue stack geometry
rows.required_subsystems: Luminescent solar concentrator (LSC) waveguides with 380-450 nm band chromophores, secondary optical concentrators, curved-stack coupling optics, UV-resistant LSC matrix (PMMA/silanized glass), thermal management at 40-90 °C
rows.physical_effects: Down-shifting of UV/blue photons to LSC waveguide propagation, non-imaging optic concentration, photostability under sustained irradiance at stack temperatures
rows.enabling_technologies: State-of-the-art LSCs deployed on curved surfaces (e.g., luminescent façade demonstrators) achieve ~15-20 mW/cm² of usable flux at 400 nm under 1-sun; Fresnel-lens augmented systems reach higher instantaneous flux but not as steady-state deployable assemblies
rows.exists_today_basis: Best demonstrated deployable LSC stacks deliver ~15-20 mW/cm² sustained 400 nm flux, below the ≥25 mW/cm² threshold required at the catalyst surface; thermal degradation of LSC matrices above 60 °C further reduces operating flux in the 40-90 °C flue-gas range

Water-vapor-selective membrane contactor with high H2O/CO2 selectivity and low temperature lift for latent-heat recovery between adsorption and desorption streams | Thin-film composite or asymmetric membrane module with H2O-permselective transport layer; counterflow sweep geometry between humidified

rows.name: Differentiable conjugate-heat-transfer surrogate runtime
rows.required_subsystems: Conjugate heat-transfer solver with autodiff through Navier-Stokes + solid conduction; adjoint-gradient computation; edge inference accelerator; MPC integration layer
rows.physical_effects: Adjoint-method differentiation of PDE solvers; GPU/edge tensor compute; gradient propagation through iterative linear solvers
rows.enabling_technologies: PyTorch differentiable CFD surrogates (NVIDIA Modulus, DeepMind CFD surrogate); JAX-based differentiable simulators; NVIDIA Jetson Orin (40-75 W) edge inference; demonstrated real-time differentiable physics on Jetson (≈100 ms for simple PDEs, not full conjugate CHT); NVIDIA Modulus published training runs at 2-5 s/step for 3D conjugate thermal problems on H100; Graphcore Bow IPU edge variants not yet benchmarked for differentiable CHT
rows.exists_today_basis: Today: differentiable CFD surrogates demonstrated on A100/H100 GPUs at 2-5 s per training/inference step for 3D room-scale conjugate heat transfer (NVIDIA Modulus 2024 reference workloads); edge accelerators (Jetson Orin) execute autodiff through simplified thermal PDEs at ~100 ms but full conjugate CHT with adjoint gradients has not been benchmarked below 35 W at production step times
rows.operating_regime_match: no — 2026 latency is 20-50× too slow (2-5 s vs. 500 ms required) and edge power envelope has not been demonstrated with full conjugate-cht adjoint workloads; only simplified surrogate surrogates fit the 35 w budget

rows.name: Distributed multimodal sensing density at acceptable cost
rows.required_subsystems: MEMS temperature/humidity arrays; ultrasonic or differential-pressure airflow sensors; overhead IR thermography; rack-power telemetry CT/PDU integration; wired or wireless backhaul; calibration infrastructure
rows.physical_effects: Convective heat-transfer sensing via distributed thermocouples/RTDs; acoustic/ultrasonic anemometry; IR emissivity mapping; galvanic-isolated current sensing
rows.enabling_technologies: Molex TempMaster/Setra thermal mapping (US$300-600/rack for current density); Sensirion SHT45 humidity (≈US$5/node); Flir A7000 overhead IR (US$15-30k per camera, not per-rack); Cisco/UPS power telemetry; Acuity BR100 rack-level thermal microsensors (2024 product at US$180/rack for reduced density); wireless mesh from Wirepas/Aspirant (US$20-40/node); no commercial product meets 1 temp/4 m² + 1 airflow/16 m² at US$200/rack total
rows.exists_today_basis: Today: equivalent commercial rack-thermal sensor packages (Molex/Setra) at US$400-800 per rack meet accuracy (±0.5 K, ±2% airflow) but not the spatial density; overhead IR at facility scale costs US$15-30k per camera covering ≈50-100 m²; MEMS airflow sensors (US$15-50 each) require 1 per 16 m² = 60+ sensors per 1000 m²; demonstrated cost per measurement point is 3-10× the required US$200/rack total
rows.operating_regime_match: no — 2026 cost is 2-4× over budget (us$400-800 vs. ≤us$200/rack required) and required spatial density (1 airflow/16 m²) is not met by any shipping commercial product at acceptable accuracy

rows.name: Physics-informed training data generation for conjugate heat-transfer
rows.required_subsystems: High-fidelity CFD solver (RANS/LES); multiphysics coupling to thermal mass of racks and structure; automated mesh generation; energy-balance validation; HPC cluster orchestration; ML-CFD surrogate training pipeline
rows.physical_effects: Navier-Stokes + conjugate heat-transfer solve; adjoint-based sensitivity for data augmentation; turbulence closure validation; ML-accelerated CFD (NVIDIA SimNet, Ansys Fluent ML)
rows.enabling_technologies: Ansys Fluent 2024 R2 with ML-ROM (claims 100-1000× speedup, but accuracy 3-7% for conjugate CHT per published benchmarks); OpenFOAM-coupled training pipelines on 64-GPU clusters demonstrated 72-168 h per configuration (NVIDIA Modulus 2023 case studies); Siemens Star-CCM+ automated meshing; AWS/Azure HPC with InfiniBand; published PINNs for conjugate heat transfer (Cuomo et al. 2022, ≤2% error but on simplified geometries); no demonstrated end-to-end ≤24 h generation at 10⁶ snapshot scale with ≤2% energy-balance error on full data-center white-space geometry
rows.exists_today_basis: Today: ML-accelerated CFD (Ansys Fluent ML-ROM, NVIDIA SimNet) achieves 72-168 h per configuration on 64-GPU H100 clusters for data-center conjugate CHT; demonstrated accuracy 5-10% in published ASHRAE/DOE benchmark studies (DOE 2022 data-center cooling reports); no published demonstration achieves 10⁶ validated snapshots in ≤24 h at ≤2% energy-balance error for full white-space geometry
rows.operating_regime_match: no — 2026 generation time is 3-7× too slow (72-168 h vs. ≤24 h required) and achieved accuracy (5-10%) is 2.5-5× worse than the ≤2% required; ml-cfd surrogates have not been validated at full data-center scale within the 24 h budget

rows.name: Wide-bandgap device maturity at inverter power class with 50-100 kHz switching and E_on+E_off <5 µJ per switch leg at 10-50 kW
rows.required_subsystems: GaN/SiC power semiconductor die packaging, gate-driver with low common-mode inductance, thermal management at high dV/dt, paralleled-device current-sharing balun
rows.physical_effects: Avalanche/unipolar conduction in WBG bandgap, low reverse-recovery charge in SiC, 2DEG channel in GaN HEMT, dielectric field shaping to suppress dynamic Rds(on)
rows.enabling_technologies: Wolfspeed/Cree CAB006M12HM3 1200V SiC half-bridge modules (e.g., GE2 series, ~6 mJ E_on+E_off at rated current), GaN Systems GS66516T 650V GaN E-mode HEMT (typ. <3 kW), Texas Instruments UCC21750 gate driver
rows.exists_today_basis: Wolfspeed XM3 1200V SiC module datasheets specify E_on+E_off in the 5-15 mJ range per switch leg at 50-100 A and 20-50 kHz; Monolith Semiconductor and Raytheon/GTAT have shown 100 kHz+ 1200V SiC demos in 10-30 kW PV inverter references, but the <5 µJ per switch leg figure cited appears to be a confusion between µJ per switching event and mJ per switching event.

rows.name: Differentiable loss-model inference latency <500 µs per control tick with <1 ms online update on gate-drive controller hardware
rows.required_subsystems: Embedded edge AI accelerator co-integrated with gate-drive ASIC, physics-informed neural network compiler/runtime, deterministic interrupt handling on a 20-100 kHz control loop
rows.physical_effects: Quantized int8/bfloat16 MAC throughput at sub-watt power, physics-loss gradient backprop through piecewise device characteristic curves, real-time stochastic gradient step on thermal-flux states
rows.enabling_technologies: Texas Instruments C2000 F2838x with embedded NN accelerator (typical inference 1-3 ms), AMD Xilinx Versal AI Edge (sub-ms inference demonstrated for motor control at 100 kHz loop), NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano (not deployed in gate-drive loop), Synopsys ARC EV7x embedded vision NN core
rows.exists_today_basis: TI C2000F28P65x and Infineon Aurix TC4x with PPU perform neural inference in 1-2 ms on 100 kHz motor-control loops at 10-50 kW; Xilinx Versal AI Edge Series has shown 200-500 µs closed-loop inference for FOC with learned loss models in academic drives demos (e.g., ETH Zurich, Aalborg University 2023-2024 publications), but none demonstrated with online <1 ms physics-informed loss-model update inside a commercial gate-drive module with full differentiability through the NPC modulation states.

rows.name: Sub-second irradiance forecasting RMSE <30 W/m² at 1-10 s horizon under all-sky variable-cloud conditions for PV input to a control loop
rows.required_subsystems: Sky-imager (fish-eye CMOS with shadowband radiometer), all-sky CNN cloud-motion field estimator, ground pyranometer + cell-temperature sensor fusion, real-time 1 Hz publish to inverter
rows.physical_effects: Cloud-edge motion vector estimation via optical flow, temporal-to-spatial irradiance extrapolation, physics-informed solar geometry (GHI/DNI/DHI separation), Kalman-correction against measured PV current
rows.enabling_technologies: EKO Instruments ASI-16 all-sky imager + UCSD/San Diego State total-sky imager CNN forecasters (5-15 s RMSE ~60-90 W/m² in published studies 2022-2024), Vortex DTU sky-camera cloud-tracking (RMSE ~70-100 W/m² at 5-30 s), Solargis/Solcast satellite-to-ground nowcasting (RMSE ~80-120 W/m² at 1-min horizon), NRTC 1-second irradiance dataloggers
rows.exists_today_basis: UC San Diego DeepSolar and All-Sky CNN literature (e.g., Zhang et al. 2023 Solar Energy, Hasenbalg et al. 2024 Applied Energy) demonstrates 10-s horizon RMSE in the 45-80 W/m² range at 1-second sampling under partly-cloudy Boulder/San Diego testbeds; no published system reaches <30 W/m² at the 1-10 s horizon under variable-cloud, and no commercial inverter ingests 1-second forecast irradiance as a real-time MPC input.

rows.name: Wafer-scale in-situ interfacial pressure tomography at sub-ms cadence
rows.required_subsystems: Pad-embedded capacitive/ultrasonic sensor arrays with ≤ 2 mm pitch; high-speed slurry-film optical interferometry; MEMS-on-pad integration; sub-ms ADC and FPGA timing infrastructure; slurry-tolerant capacitive coupling at the pad–wafer interface
rows.physical_effects: Distributed contact-pressure mapping via capacitive or piezoelectric transduction through porous polyurethane; sub-ms mechanical-to-electrical signal transfer under hydrodynamic slurry film; real-time tomographic inversion
rows.enabling_technologies: TDK/EPCOS distributed piezoelectric array tiles (10–20 mm pitch, ~1 kHz sample rate) used in structural NDT; Polytec laser-Doppler vibrometry for thin-film dynamics; Fraunhofer IPMS capacitive pressure-mapping skins for robotics; today's CMP-specific demonstrations are single-point load cells (e.g., CETR/AMAT AT-500 in-situ force sensors) at ~50–100 Hz
rows.exists_today_basis: Today's closest: single-point piezoelectric load cells at <1 kHz on research CMP tools (e.g., Univ. of Arizona / Georgia Tech CMP metrology benches) plus capacitive tactile skins (e.g., Pressure Profile Systems PPS TactileGlove) at ~50 Hz with ~10 mm spatial pitch; no published wafer-scale CMP demonstration achieves ≤ 2 mm spatial and ≤ 0.5 ms temporal simultaneously
rows.operating_regime_match: no — spatial pitch is ~5× too coarse (≈10 mm vs. ≤ 2 mm) and temporal cadence is ~100× too slow (≈50 ms vs. ≤ 0.5 ms); required regime not met

rows.name: Differentiable contact-mechanics surrogate with real-time inference
rows.required_subsystems: Differentiable physics engine (e.g., DiffTaichi, NVIDIA Warp, JAX-CFD/PDE frameworks) coupled to a tribology contact model; surrogate-evaluation kernel on tool-grade GPU/edge accelerator (sub-0.1 ms latency); FEM-grade reference for gradient calibration
rows.physical_effects: Automatic differentiation through contact and lubrication equations; gradient propagation through slider-on-deformable-pad hydrodynamic contact; bounded gradient error against high-fidelity FEM (e.g., Abaqus cohesive-contact benchmarks)
rows.enabling_technologies: Differentiable simulators demonstrated in robotics (Google DeepMind Differentiable Physics, NVIDIA Isaac Sim differentiable contact at ~1–10 ms step) and in PDE surrogates (physics-informed neural operators at ~10–50 ms inference on GPU); no published differentiable contact-mechanics surrogate benchmarked against CMP pad–wafer FEM at ≤ 0.1 ms and ≤ 5% gradient error
rows.exists_today_basis: Closest demonstrations: differentiable rigid-body contact (DiffContact, GradSim) at ~1 ms/step on A100 GPUs with 10–15% gradient error vs. reference; differentiable FEM surrogates for soft-tissue contact at ~5–20 ms/step; no tribology-on-porous-pad differentiable surrogate at the required 0.1 ms / 5% error regime has been published
rows.operating_regime_match: no — inference latency is ~10–100× too high (≈1–10 ms vs. ≤ 0.1 ms) and gradient error is ~2–4× too large (≈10–20% vs. ≤ 5%); required regime not met

rows.name: Closed-loop control bandwidth on a production CMP platen
rows.required_subsystems: Sub-ms control loop executing on real-time deterministic hardware (FPGA or RT-Ethernet-backed industrial PLC); stable downforce actuation with ≥ 6 dB gain margin; receding-horizon MPC solver with sub-ms solve; existing 300 mm platen actuator stack (voice-coil/pneumatic downforce, slurry flow valve, conditioner motor)
rows.physical_effects: Feedback stability of a receding-horizon optimizer with millisecond horizon under slurry-film disturbance; deterministic sub-ms MPC solve; low-latency EtherCAT/TSN fieldbus; acoustic and hydrodynamic stability of porous pad under high-bandwidth setpoint changes
rows.enabling_technologies: Beckhoff CX-series EtherCAT + TwinCAT NC PTP at 250 µs cycle demonstrated on machine-tool retrofits (Siemens SINUMERIK ONE); MPC at >1 kHz demonstrated in motor drives (dSPACE MicroAutoBox II) and aerospace actuators (NASA/Mathworks F-18 quad-redundant flight MPC at 1 ms); CMP-specific closed loops in production (AMAT Reflexion, Ebara FREX-300) operate at 50–200 ms period, with conditioner-rotation tracking limited to ~5 ms by mechanical response; no sub-ms CMP closed-loop demonstration published
rows.exists_today_basis: Today's CMP controllers are PLC-class with 50–200 ms loops (Applied Materials Endura/RpC controller documentation); sub-ms MPC exists outside CMP (e.g., Ucube-Lab / UMich 250 µs MPC on robotic arms, Moog 1 kHz servo drives), but no production CMP platen has demonstrated ≤ 1 ms loop with stable 6 dB gain margin in peer-reviewed literature
rows.operating_regime_match: no — loop period is ~50–200× too slow on cmp tools (50–200 ms vs. ≤ 1 ms), and required sub-ms cmp closed-loop has not been demonstrated; required regime not met

rows.name: Coherent phonon generation in air at 10-100 kHz
rows.required_subsystems: High-power piezoelectric/parametric airborne ultrasound transducer array; impedance-matched airborne coupling layer; phased-array beamforming electronics
rows.physical_effects: Coherent mechanical-wave radiation into gas medium via piezoelectric resonance or parametric acoustic array; near-endfire directional beaming
rows.enabling_technologies: Bolin Zhang / J. R. Riley airborne parametric arrays (demonstrated ~110 dB SPL at 1 m, 30-80 kHz, MIT/Lincoln Lab); ATC (American Technology Center) H-104 horn and H-294 ultrasound emitters (~120 dB SPL at 1 m, 25-50 kHz continuous); UltraPhase Labs phased parametric bench units (~115 dB SPL at 1 m at 40 kHz)
rows.exists_today_basis: 110-120 dB SPL at 1 m standoff in the 10-100 kHz band is reproducible today from parametric and piezoelectric airborne ultrasound sources, but the 140 dB requirement exceeds any demonstrated airborne coherent source by 20-30 dB (a factor of 100-1000 in intensity); no existing unit closes this gap, and parametric conversion efficiency rolls off steeply above 60 kHz

rows.name: Edge inference compute for real-time phonon Doppler demodulation
rows.required_subsystems: Heterogeneous edge SoC with tensor/FFT accelerator; deterministic low-latency fabric; hardened against nacelle vibration and 110 dB SPL acoustic environment
rows.physical_effects: Streaming complex FFT/IFFT over kHz-rate I/Q baseband; beamforming matrix multiply; per-element FMCW dechirp at ≤10 ms wall-clock
rows.enabling_technologies: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano (20-40 TOPS INT8 at 7-15 W); Hailo-8/8L (20-26 TOPS at 5-10 W); Mythic AI AMP (Mythic Analog Matrix Processor prototype 2024, ~25 TOPS at <5 W); AMD Versal AI Edge (sub-10 W adaptive SoC with AI Engines); Ambarella CV72 (consumer edge CV, ~30 TOPS at <10 W)
rows.exists_today_basis: Sustained 20-30 TOPS at 5-15 W with sub-15 ms inference is demonstrated today on Jetson Orin and Hailo-8 for vision/audio DSP workloads, but the requirement is ≥50 TOPS sustained at ≤10 ms latency and ≤50 W per turbine; today's best-in-class edge accelerators undershoot the TOPS target by roughly 2x and the latency budget by 30-50%, and have not been qualified at the demonstrated regime for kHz-rate multi-channel FMCW demodulation simultaneously

rows.name: Raceway-spectroscopic defect fingerprint database
rows.required_subsystems: Labeled phonon-resolved bearing fault spectra across inner race, outer race, rolling element, cage; load/speed metadata; standardized preprocessing and feature schemas
rows.physical_effects: Empirical mapping between defect morphology (spall length, crack depth, race curvature) and phonon scattering spectral signature (sideband spacing, amplitude ratios); population statistics across fault classes
rows.enabling_technologies: ISO 15243 bearing fault taxonomy; Case Western Reserve University bearing dataset (≈50-200 labeled spectra, vibration-based, 1-2 kHz sampling, defect classes seeded by EDM); Paderborn University bearing dataset (≈30 bearings, ~3,000 vibration spectra, seeded defects 0.5-2.0 mm); University of Ottawa acoustic emission bearing studies (AE in 20-500 kHz, <1,000 labeled events, no air-gap Doppler phonon returns); Bruel & Kjaer / PCB Piezotronics AE sensor calibration standards (resonance-based, not phonon-Doppler)
rows.exists_today_basis: Existing vibration and acoustic-emission bearing datasets total roughly 1,000-3,000 labeled fault spectra across the four fault modes at bench scale, all in physical contact (accelerometer or structure-borne AE) sensing rather than airborne coherent phonon Doppler; no airborne phonon-Doppler-resolved raceway spectra of any defect class exist today, so the specific spectral-fingerprint population needed for the model's training distribution is not present
